messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Spanish, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------| | Nel | “in the middle of” – locative prepositional phrase introducing the central point | **En** (preposition, locative, governs a noun phrase in the accusative) – literal back‑translation: “in” | | mezzo | The central point of a span; here the midpoint of life’s journey | **el medio** (noun, masculine singular, definite article) – literal back‑translation: “the middle” | | del | “of the” – genitive linking the road to the larger context | **del** (contraction of *de* + *el*, preposition + definite article) – literal back‑translation: “of the” | | cammin | The route or way that one travels on; metaphor for life’s course | **camino** (noun, masculine singular) – literal back‑translation: “road” | | di | Marks possession/association between “road” and “our life” | **de** (preposition, genitive) – literal back‑translation: “of” | | nostra | Belonging to the speaker and companions; collective ownership of life | **nuestra** (adjective, feminine singular, agrees with *vida*) – literal back‑translation: “our” | | vita | The span of existence of the speaker; the overall journey | **vida** (noun, feminine singular) – literal back‑translation: “life” | | mi | Reflexive pronoun, 1st‑person singular; part of the reflexive construction | **me** (reflexive pronoun, 1st person singular, object) – literal back‑translation: “myself” | | ritrovai | The act of discovering or realizing one’s own state | **encontré** (verb, 1st person singular, preterite indicative) – literal back‑translation: “I found” | | per | Indicates interior location inside something | **por** (preposition, directional, marks “within”) – literal back‑translation: “through/within” | | una | Introduces a non‑specific noun | **una** (indefinite article, feminine singular) – literal back‑translation: “a” | | selva | A densely wooded area; here metaphorically dark and confusing | **selva** (noun, feminine singular) – literal back‑translation: “forest/wood” | | oscura | Lacking light; conveys gloom and uncertainty | **oscura** (adjective, feminine singular, agrees with *selva*) – literal back‑translation: “dark” | | ché | Introduces a causal clause explaining the previous state | **porque** (conjunction, causal) – literal back‑translation: “because/for” | | la | Specifies the particular way being spoken of | **la** (definite article, feminine singular) – literal back‑translation: “the” | | diritta | Correct or proper; the morally/technically correct path | **recta** (adjective, feminine singular, agrees with *vía*) – literal back‑translation: “right/straight” | | via | The correct route or method of proceeding | **vía** (noun, feminine singular) – literal back‑translation: “way” | | era | Past state of being; forms the passive perfect with *smarrita* | **había sido** (auxiliary *haber* in imperfect 3rd person singular + past participle *sido*) – literal back‑translation: “had been” | | smarrita | The state of being lost or not found; here the correct way is absent | **perdida** (adjective/past participle, feminine singular, agrees with *vía*) – literal back‑translation: “lost/missed” |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Spanish components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 1: En el medio del camino de nuestra vida / En el medio del camino de nuestra vida ahora / En el medio del camino de nuestra vida entonces - Line 2: Me encontré por una selva oscura / Me encontré por una selva oscura ahora / Me encontré por una selva oscura entonces - Line 3: Porque la recta vía había sido perdida / Porque la recta vía había sido perdida ya / Porque la recta vía había sido perdida entonces

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Spanish lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

Source Line: 1 Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita Line Inventory: - En el medio del camino de nuestra vida Assembly Notes: - none Target Text: En el medio del camino de nuestra vida
Source Line: 2 mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, Line Inventory: - Me encontré por una selva oscura Assembly Notes: - none Target Text: Me encontré por una selva oscura,
Source Line: 3 ché la diritta via era smarrita. Line Inventory: - Porque la recta vía había sido perdida Assembly Notes: - none Target Text: Porque la recta vía había sido perdida.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 1 - Target Text (from Step 4): En el medio del camino de nuestra vida - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): In the middle of the road of our life - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): Midway upon the road of our life - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 2 - Target Text (from Step 4): Me encontré por una selva oscura, - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): I found myself through a dark forest, - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): I found myself within a dark wood, - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **FAIL**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK** - Corrected Target Text: Me encontré en una selva oscura,
- Line #: 3 - Target Text (from Step 4): Porque la recta vía había sido perdida. - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): Because the straight way had been lost. - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): for the right way had been missed. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
**FINAL STATUS:** UNVERIFIED (fails: Line 2)
```text En el medio del camino de nuestra vida Me encontré en una selva oscura, Porque la recta vía había sido perdida. ```
